question: A 5-year-old child requires inhalational induction of anaesthesia. Which agent is preferred, and what pharmacokinetic property makes it suitable?

answers.text: Sevoflurane — low blood:gas partition coefficient (0.65) gives rapid onset, and its non-pungent odour ensures smooth induction without airway irritation

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. A low blood:gas partition coefficient means rapid equilibration between alveolar gas and arterial blood, producing fast induction and recovery. Sevoflurane's pleasant smell is critical for mask induction in uncooperative children.

answers.text: Halothane — lowest MAC (highest potency) ensures deepest anaesthesia with minimal drug quantity

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Halothane is potent (low MAC) but carries risks of hepatotoxicity (halothane hepatitis) and is a potent trigger of malignant hyperthermia. It has largely been replaced by sevoflurane for paediatric use.

answers.text: Desflurane — lowest blood:gas partition coefficient (0.42) gives the fastest onset of all volatile agents

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Desflurane does have the lowest blood:gas partition coefficient, but it is extremely pungent and causes airway irritation (coughing, laryngospasm, bronchospasm). It is never used for inhalational induction — only for maintenance.

answers.text: Nitrous oxide — safest agent with analgesic properties and no cardiac depression

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Nitrous oxide has a MAC >100% — it cannot produce surgical anaesthesia alone. It is used as an adjunct to reduce the MAC of other agents, not as a sole induction agent.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember: speed of induction is governed by the blood:gas partition coefficient (lower = faster), while potency is measured by MAC (lower = more potent). For paediatric induction, patient acceptance (odour, airway irritation) is equally important.
Sevoflurane combines a low blood:gas partition coefficient (fast onset/recovery) with a non-irritant, pleasant odour — making it the gold standard for inhalational induction in children.
